items: pH: at pH about 6 to 7.5 HOCl predominates and disinfection is most effective; above pH 7.5 OCl- predominates, less effective but still disinfecting.
Chlorine dose: the more chlorine, the more effective the disinfection; enough must be added to give sufficient HOCl and OCl- to kill the bacteria.
Contact time: the water must stay in contact with the chlorine long enough for the disinfectants to penetrate and kill bacteria, viruses and protozoa.

blocks.prompt: Explain the chemical principles behind chlorine as a water disinfectant, with equations, and list the factors that affect it (exercise Q.2k; Quick Check 13.6b).
blocks.explanation: Chlorine hydrolyses, Cl2 + H2O giving HCl + HOCl, and HOCl partly ionises to H+ + OCl-; the neutral HOCl enters microbial cells and both species oxidise proteins, enzymes and nucleic acids, killing the organisms. Effectiveness depends on pH (HOCl dominates at 6 to 7.5), on the chlorine dose, and on the contact time.

items: Disinfection depends on pH (HOCl at 6-7.5 most effective, OCl- above 7.5), chlorine dose and contact time.
